answer: Each agent locks a stake before it may vote or earn rewards. At random checkpoints the protocol samples live identities: a node at the wharf pays a bond while another on the terrace verifies the same ledger, and each is matched to its bond. Clones sharing one budget gain no extra weight because the stake is divided, never duplicated. When a tide of accusations exposes double-signing, the whole bond is slashed, so spoofing a crowd costs real capital rather than new names.
